card.title: Order of Business
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the person who decides what happens in what order. Redirect every interruption into the approved sequence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss the kitchen fire, may I approve last week's minutes?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The minutes are in the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we must establish whether anyone remembers them.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I remember voting to replace the extinguisher.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We can begin with matters arising.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 puts minute approval before the fire, A3 substitutes remembered minutes when access fails, and A5 routes the extinguisher decision into matters arising.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's minutes-in-kitchen fact causes A3's memory inquiry; B4's remembered extinguisher vote supplies A5's next approved agenda category.

relationship.evidence: B2 points out the blocked document and B4 offers information relevant to both the minutes and current emergency.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's practical memory to advance the sequence, though the external situation develops only slightly.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a kitchen fire during a meeting and the priority conflict over minutes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's matters-arising phrase is particularly earned by B4's previous extinguisher vote and the current fire.
